summary: Thorough, transparent preregistered experiment and full artifact bundle comparing a deterministic template baseline to a single‑pass LLM configuration pipeline under preregistered shared‑candidate semantics. The run, analysis, and disclosure are well archived; the degenerate confirmatory outcome (both conditions 120/120) is correctly reported and appropriately attributed to the preregistered shared_initial_candidate design and templated tasks. The manuscript is reproducible and suitably cautious about generalization.
optional_revisions: Add an explicit, single‑sentence caution at the top of the Abstract and again as the first sentence of the Conclusion that the confirmatory paired test used shared_initial_candidate semantics and therefore does not assess independent LLM generative robustness (this is present in the paper but placing a very short, high‑visibility caution reduces risk of misreading).

Provide a compact table (1/2 page or smaller) in Methods or Appendix listing the exact canonical artifact paths and SHA‑256 hashes cited in the Disclosure so readers can immediately locate the key files used to justify the degenerate outcome (e.g., execution/responses/*-shared-initial.txt and execution/scoring/*-guarded.json entries referenced in Results).

In Related Work, add one brief explicit comparison sentence contrasting this preregistered artifact‑anchored protocol with prior LLM→NetOps evaluations that used independent per‑condition sampling, to clarify the distinct experimental question addressed here.
